question: Should Discord Activity support be rebuilt under the Canvas and Discord plugin contracts with fail-closed Activity auth, continued through the newer overlapping PR after repair, or paused until maintainers settle the Activity security model?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses Gateway authorization, token transport, plugin config ownership, operator upgrade behavior, and two overlapping maintainer-labeled PRs, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials or a verifiable exchange, remove URL tokens, bound fanout, and add proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause Activity support
options.body: Keep both branches as design context until maintainers decide whether the Activity bridge belongs in the Canvas plugin, Discord plugin, or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials or a verifiable exchange, remove URL tokens, bound fanout, and add proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved decision is the Canvas/Gateway auth and plugin config boundary introduced by the Canvas plugin migration history.
